title: One notion to rule them all
intro_md: Glossary and notation for the plant–AMF interaction-spectrum model. One notation is used in every tab, formula, slider label and hover text.

**Competition convention:** α_ij = effect of species j on species i. So α_MZ = effect of the cheater Z on the mutualist M (paper c₁), and α_ZM = effect of M on Z (paper c₂). In the model they appear as dM/dt = b_M·H·M − d_M·M(1 + e_M·M + α_MZ·Z) and dZ/dt = b_Z·H·Z − d_Z·Z(1 + e_Z·Z + α_ZM·M).
**Source column:** short reference of the paper a symbol comes from; blank = introduced here or a generic term. **Source symbol** = the symbol used in that source.
tabs_note: Tabs: ① static physiology, ② population dynamics, ③ cheater fungus, ④ plant sanctions, ⑤ parameter space.

symbols.name: Host density
symbols.notes: Plant population density.

symbols.name: Equilibrium host density
symbols.notes: Long-run host density with the fungi present.

symbols.name: Host density without fungi
symbols.notes: Logistic growth to K_P; at equilibrium H_NM = K_P.

symbols.name: Mutualist symbiont density
symbols.notes: Fungus that can provide benefit (raises host capacity via γ).

symbols.name: Cheater density
symbols.notes: Fungus that provides no benefit (γ_Z = 0 in the paper) but competes for the host.

symbols.name: Phosphorus / soil fertility (host carrying capacity without fungi)
symbols.notes: Higher K_P = more fertile. Conceptually increases with soil-available P, S (tab ①); no quantitative mapping K_P(S) is implied.

symbols.name: Benefit coefficient
symbols.notes: Increase in host carrying capacity per mutualist: capacity = K_P + γM.

symbols.name: Benefit coefficient of the cheater
symbols.notes: 0 = pure cheater (paper). Capacity becomes K_P + γM + γ_Z Z.

symbols.name: Cost to host per symbiont
symbols.notes: Carbon or other cost (exploitation) per unit mutualist / cheater.

symbols.name: Competition coefficients between M and Z
symbols.notes: Convention α_ij = effect of j on i: α_MZ = effect of the cheater Z on the mutualist M (paper c₁), α_ZM = effect of M on Z (paper c₂). As in the paper they act inside the density-dependent death term, d_M M(1 + e_M M + α_MZ Z).

symbols.name: Host intrinsic growth rate
symbols.notes: Per-capita host growth at low density.

symbols.name: Symbiont growth rate on the host
symbols.notes: Per-capita fungal growth per unit host. The paper assumes b_M/d_M > b_Z/d_Z (mutualist grows faster).

symbols.name: Symbiont self-limitation (density-dependent death)
symbols.notes: Strength of intraspecific competition.

symbols.name: Equilibrium mutualist density
symbols.notes: Interior equilibrium of the host–mutualist model (solved analytically). Pulse-mutualistic iff M* < r/2a_M − K_P/2γ (vertex height); equilibrium-mutualistic iff M* < r/a_M − K_P/γ.

symbols.name: Pulse-criterion value ∂(dH/dt)/∂M at equilibrium
symbols.notes: = H*[rγH*/(K_P+γM*)² − a_M]; > 0 mutualism, < 0 parasitism.

symbols.name: Sufficient parasitism bound
symbols.notes: If K_P > γr/a_M the vertex of the host isocline lies below M = 0 and both criteria are always parasitic. Only sufficient: the actual switch points (see M*) lie at lower K_P.

symbols.name: Symbiont carrying capacities for invasion criteria
symbols.notes: λ_i^(X) = (1/e_i)((b_i/d_i) H̄^(X) − 1), host fixed at the X-only equilibrium. Z invades the M-only equilibrium iff α_ZM < e_Z λ_Z^(M)/λ_M^(M); M invades the Z-only equilibrium iff α_MZ < e_M λ_M^(Z)/λ_Z^(Z).

symbols.name: Sanction strength
symbols.notes: 0 = no discrimination; 1 = rewards fully proportional to benefit delivered.

symbols.name: Baseline reward / recognition noise
symbols.notes: Added to every fungus’ benefit before rewards are computed; higher = plant tells partners apart less well.

symbols.name: Perceived benefit per fungus and its abundance-weighted mean
symbols.notes: q_M = γ + q_0, q_Z = γ_Z + q_0, q̄ = (M q_M + Z q_Z)/(M + Z).

symbols.name: Reward weights (carbon per unit fungus, relative)
symbols.notes: w_i = (1 − s) + s q_i/q̄; M w_M + Z w_Z = M + Z, so sanctions redistribute the reward per unit fungus without changing its total. The host’s carbon drain a_M w_M M + a_Z w_Z Z is not conserved when a_M ≠ a_Z. Multiply both a_i and b_i.

symbols.name: Mutualist share of the fungal community
symbols.notes: Used for mixed colonisation and the sanctions map.

symbols.name: Cheater cooperativeness and community cooperativeness
symbols.notes: Bridge to tab ①: φ_mix = [M φ + Z φ_Z]/(M + Z) replaces φ in the static model.

symbols.name: Commensalism band
symbols.notes: |response| ≤ ε counts as commensal (neutral). Used for MGR, ln(H*/K_P) and Δ_F.

symbols.name: Soil-available phosphorus
symbols.notes: Drives root and hyphal P uptake in tab ①. Relation: higher S ↔ higher fertility K_P in tabs ②–④ (conceptual only).
symbols.src: cf. Hochberg et al. 2000; Schwartz & Hoeksema 1998

symbols.name: Maximum and actual carbon fixation
symbols.notes: A = A_max L.

symbols.name: Phosphorus requirement per unit biomass
symbols.notes: Higher = more P-hungry plant.

symbols.name: Root P uptake: maximum rate and half-saturation constant
symbols.notes: Michaelis–Menten; K_r is a half-saturation constant, not a carrying capacity (unrelated to K_P). Subscript r = root (unrelated to growth rate r).

symbols.name: Hyphal P uptake: maximum rate and half-saturation constant
symbols.notes: K_f < K_r: hyphae scavenge better at low P.

symbols.name: Root and hyphal P uptake rates
symbols.notes: U = u S/(K + S).

symbols.name: Fungal own P need
symbols.notes: Hyphal P the fungus keeps before passing any on: transfer = cφ·max(U_f − U_0, 0). At very low S nothing is passed, so MGR ≈ ln(1 − ρc) < 0 and MGR peaks at intermediate S. U_0 = 0 recovers the model without a hump.

symbols.name: Colonisation
symbols.notes: Fraction of root length colonised.

symbols.name: Cooperativeness of the (mutualist) fungus
symbols.notes: Share of fungal P (above the fungus's own need U_0) passed to the plant.

symbols.name: Carbon cost
symbols.notes: Fraction of fixed C per unit colonisation passed to the fungus.

symbols.name: Root-pathway suppression
symbols.notes: Down-regulation of direct root uptake in colonised roots.

symbols.name: Phosphorus acquired by the mycorrhizal (AM) / non-mycorrhizal (NM) plant
symbols.notes: P here always means phosphorus (never a fungal density).

symbols.name: Carbon available for growth (AM / NM plant)
symbols.notes: C_AM = A(1 − cκ).

symbols.name: Plant biomass with / without mycorrhiza
symbols.notes: B = softmin(Y C, P/θ). Renamed from M_AM/M_NM to avoid a clash with mutualist density M.

symbols.name: Co-limitation sharpness
symbols.notes: softmin(x,y) = (x⁻ⁿ + y⁻ⁿ)^(−1/n); n → ∞ is the strict Liebig minimum.

symbols.name: Mycorrhizal growth response
symbols.notes: ln(B_AM/B_NM). In tabs ②–④ the analogous population-level response is ln(H*/K_P).

symbols.name: Effective exchange rate
symbols.notes: Extra P gained per unit C paid: (cφU_f − ρcU_r)/(cκA). Market view after Schwartz & Hoeksema 1998.

symbols.name: Fungal growth, its yield, P requirement and own C uptake
symbols.notes: F = Y_f softmin(cκA + β_f, (cU_f − cφ·max(U_f − U_0, 0))/θ_f). Speculative.

symbols.name: Reference fungal fitness and fungal response
symbols.notes: Δ_F = ln(F/F_ref); F_ref = fitness with a reference partner (AMF are obligate). The sign of Δ_F, and so the 2-D label, depends on the choice of F_ref.

terms.definition: Both partners are better off together. Here: the plant’s response (MGR or ln(H*/K_P)) is above +ε. Colour: green.
One partner gains while the other is essentially unaffected; here the plant response lies within ±ε. Colour: grey.
The fungus gains at the plant’s expense: the plant response is below −ε. Colour: red.
Other sign combinations on the plant × fungus plane (tab ①): (0,−) amensalism, (−,−) competition.
How much bigger (or smaller) a mycorrhizal plant is than a non-mycorrhizal one, on a log scale: ln(B_AM/B_NM). MGR = 0.1 ≈ 10% bigger.
Growth is set by the scarcest resource (here carbon or phosphorus). The smooth version (softmin) lets both matter near the switch point.
Which resource currently sets growth. A P-limited plant profits from fungal P; a C-limited plant mainly feels the carbon it pays.
How much P the plant gets per unit carbon given (T_eff). Trade is beneficial only within a window of exchange rates (biological market view).
The density a population settles at when resources limit it. K_P is the host’s carrying capacity without fungi and stands in for soil fertility.
Long-term experiment: grow the plant with and without the fungus until both settle; mutualism if H* > K_P (ln(H*/K_P) > ε).
Short-term experiment: at equilibrium, add a few more fungi; mutualism if this speeds up host growth (J_HM > 0). Can disagree with the equilibrium criterion.
Curve in the phase plane where one population does not change. Equilibria are where the host and fungus isoclines cross.
The peak of the host isocline. An equilibrium below it is pulse-mutualistic, above it pulse-parasitic.
A fungus that takes host carbon but delivers no (or little) benefit (Z, γ_Z ≈ 0).
Can a rare fungus increase when the other fungus is established? If both can invade they coexist; if neither can, the outcome depends on who arrives first (bistability).
Both fungi persist / one drives the other out.

The plant gives more carbon to partners that deliver more P and less to cheaters (s = strength). Here modelled as a redistribution of the reward per unit fungus; total carbon paid still changes when partners differ in cost.
Choosing or favouring better partners in a biological market (Hammerstein & Noë 2016); sanctions are one mechanism.
All parameter values are illustrative and in relative units; the app shows qualitative patterns, not calibrated predictions.

The fraction of Latin-hypercube samples, drawn across a tab's slider ranges, that fall in an outcome class (mutualism, commensalism, parasitism, or 'cannot persist'). Shares describe that slider box, not frequencies in nature; they change if the ranges or the sampling scale change. Colour: as in the other tabs (green / grey / red).

How strongly a parameter shifts the predicted outcome class, measured as random-forest permutation importance on the same Latin-hypercube sample (scaled so the top parameter is 1). It identifies which sliders drive the classification, not a causal effect size.
